headline: Reaction time is response speed—how quickly you can perceive and act on changes
universal_truth: Fast response requires preparation; you can only act quickly on what you're ready to perceive
fun_facts: Human reaction time is about 250 milliseconds—a quarter second to respond to what you perceive
Athletes train reaction time like any skill—anticipation is trainable
Reaction time slows with fatigue, age, and distraction—it's not constant
discussion_questions: Where does slow reaction cost you opportunities?
What would you respond to faster if you could?
How does preparation affect your response speed?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Something changes. How fast can you respond? Reaction time is the gap between stimulus and action—how quickly you perceive and act. In fast-moving situations, that quarter-second matters enormously.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: We think reaction time is fixed, but it's highly trainable. What determines how fast you can respond?

options.text: Reaction time depends on preparation—anticipating possibilities, pre-loading responses, and staying alert; you respond fastest to what you're ready for
options.response: Yes. Raw reaction time is limited by biology. But anticipation effectively eliminates the lag. Experts aren't faster—they're more prepared. They know what to look for.
Natural speed varies, but preparation and anticipation matter more than raw speed...

q1.title: Anticipation Beats Speed
q1.script: Athletes seem supernaturally fast because they anticipate—they start responding before the event. Anticipation effectively reduces reaction time to near-zero.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Anticipation Beats Speed"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Pre-Loaded Responses
q2.script: If you've decided what to do in advance, you just need to trigger the response. Pre-loading decisions eliminates deliberation time. Preparation is compressed reaction.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Readiness Matters
q3.script: You respond faster when alert, rested, and focused. Fatigue and distraction slow you down. Reaction time isn't fixed—it varies with your state. Stay ready.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Fast response requires preparation. You can only act quickly on what you're ready to perceive. Anticipate and prepare.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 308. Tomorrow, we'll explore why water keeps you working—hydration. Until then, consider what you should be more prepared to respond to.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Response Preparation - What Should You Be Ready For?
growTrack.activity: What situations would benefit from faster response? What can you anticipate? What decisions can you pre-load? Preparation is the key to speed. Decide in advance.
